hsdd.definition: A diagnosis for low or absent sexual desire that causes marked distress or problems in a relationship. It only applies when another illness, a medicine or problems in the relationship do not explain it.

female-sexual-arousal-disorder.definition: An older diagnosis for women whose body does not become sexually aroused, or stays aroused too briefly, which causes distress. Newer manuals merge it with low desire.

mc4r.definition: A receptor for melanocortin hormones, found mainly on nerve cells in the brain. It helps control appetite and is linked to sexual function and blood pressure.

medial-preoptic-area.definition: A small region at the front of the hypothalamus in the brain. In animals it is important for sexual behaviour.

dopamine.definition: A chemical messenger between nerve cells. It plays a part in motivation, reward and movement.

sympathetic-nervous-system.definition: The part of the nervous system that gets the body ready for action. It can narrow blood vessels and raise blood pressure.

hyperpigmentation.definition: Patches of skin or gums that turn darker than the area around them, because pigment cells make more pigment there.

gingiva.definition: The medical word for the gums: the pink tissue around the teeth.

hypertension.definition: Blood pressure that is too high most of the time. It usually causes no symptoms, but over years it raises the risk of heart attack and stroke.

systolic-blood-pressure.definition: Blood pressure has two numbers. The top (systolic) number is the pressure when the heart pumps; the bottom (diastolic) number is the pressure between beats. Both are measured in mmHg.

ambulatory-blood-pressure-monitoring.definition: Blood pressure measured automatically by a cuff worn during normal life, often every 15 to 30 minutes for a day or more.

cardiovascular-disease.definition: Disease of the heart or blood vessels, such as a past heart attack, angina, heart failure or a stroke.

autoinjector.definition: A pen with a fixed, pre-filled amount of medicine and a hidden needle. Pressed against the skin, it injects the dose by itself.

fsfi.definition: A questionnaire that women fill in about their sex life over the past four weeks. Its desire part has two questions and gives a score from 1.2 to 6.

fsds-dao.definition: A questionnaire about how much distress a woman feels about her sexual desire, arousal and orgasm. Item 13 asks how often low desire bothered her, from 0 (never) to 4 (always).

satisfying-sexual-event.definition: In sexual-health trials, a sexual encounter that the participant herself rated as satisfying, counted in a diary.

responder-analysis.definition: A way of reporting a trial by counting how many people improved by at least an amount judged to matter, instead of only the average change.

crossover-trial.definition: A trial in which each person receives both the treatment and the comparison (often a placebo), one after the other in random order, so they act as their own control.

functional-mri.definition: A brain scan that shows which brain areas become more or less active during a task, by tracking changes in blood flow.

expression-of-concern.definition: A notice by a journal that it has serious doubts about a published paper, for example about its data, while it looks into it. It is a warning, not yet a retraction.

retraction.definition: The formal withdrawal of a published paper by the journal, because its results can no longer be trusted.

pde5-inhibitor.definition: A group of medicines for erection problems, such as sildenafil (Viagra). They help blood flow into the penis during sexual arousal.

erectile-dysfunction.definition: When a man often cannot get or keep an erection firm enough for sex.

naltrexone.definition: A medicine that blocks opioid receptors. Taken by mouth, it helps people stay off alcohol or opioids.

antiemetic.definition: A medicine that prevents or eases feeling sick and vomiting.

acute-hepatitis.definition: Inflammation of the liver that starts suddenly. Signs can include yellow skin or eyes, dark urine and feeling very unwell.

premenopausal.definition: Before the menopause: a woman who still has periods.

pregnancy-registry.definition: A study that collects information on women who used a medicine while pregnant, and on their babies, to find out whether the medicine causes harm.

postmarketing-requirement.definition: A study that a regulator orders a company to carry out after a medicine is approved, to answer safety questions that were still open.

norleucine.definition: A building block similar to the amino acid leucine, but with a straight side chain. Human proteins do not use it; chemists add it to make peptides more stable.

odds-ratio.definition: A number that compares the chance of something happening in two groups. An odds ratio of 1 means no difference; above 1 means it happened more often in the first group.

lactam-bridge.definition: A chemical link that joins two side chains of the same peptide, closing it into a ring.
